Executive Summary
This Risk Management Plan (RMP) covers the Texas Deepwater Terminal located at 2555 Penn City Road, Houston, TX 77015, specifically addressing onsite operations involving Normal Pentane, Isopentane, and Isopentane/n-Pentane Blends in compliance with EPA 40 CFR Part 68.

Latitude/Longitude (Source): 29.753144, -95.154671

The management of the Texas Deepwater Terminal in Houston, Texas, recognizes and shares the communitys interest in the safe operation of our facility. We have completed this report under the U.S. Environmental Protection Agencys (EPA) Risk Management Program requirements to communicate our efforts to achieve a safe workplace.

The terminal handles Pentane and Isopentane by a process called transloading, or transferring product from vessel to vessel for further transport by customer carrier. Pentane and Isopentane are materials covered under the U.S. Environmental Protection Agencys Risk Management program regulations. The terminal follows these regulations, as well as the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administrations Process Safety Management standard (PSM) to ensure the safe handling, use, and storage of these chemicals and other potentially hazardous chemicals. The terminal is a new operation and thus has had no prior incident history.

Our corporate environmental, health, and safety (EHS) policy and requirements promote the overall safety of this terminal, its employees, contractors, and the public. This policy includes risk reduction programs that provide assurance for the safe management of process risks to prevent environmental, health and safety incidents and to protect the workplace, the community and the environment. These programs enable the terminal to prevent the occurrence, or minimize the consequences of significant releases of these chemicals.

It is Texas Deepwater Partners policy to conduct business in accordance with all applicable laws, regulations, and permits, and to promote a safe workplace and a qu

ality environment. Each employee is trained and required to comply strictly with this policy. We do not allow production goals or financial objectives to override safety and environmental concerns.

Also, it is Texas Deepwater Partners policy to lead by example so that other companies, including vendors and suppliers, are similarly interested in protecting the health and safety of employees and safeguarding the environment. We are committed to the spirit as well as the letter of our EHS policy and promote, throughout the organization, responsibility and accountability for strict compliance with that policy. Texas Deepwater Partners employees whose actions in the performance of their duties may affect the environment and/or public health are trained sufficiently to permit them to comply strictly with our EHS policy.

In conducting our business, we continue to seek and implement cost-effective methods to reduce the EHS impact of our operations. We integrate EHS considerations into our business planning and decision-making processes, including process research and development. Our continuous EHS improvement goals include pollution prevention and resource conservation. We ask our contractors to adopt EHS standards, ethics, and policies similar to our own, and we give preference to suppliers that do so.

We encourage our employees, customers, and the public to share with us their EHS concerns. We continually talk with local authorities in the communities in which we operate to share ideas about preventing incidents with materials we use or store.

Covered Chemicals
Chemicals subject to RMP regulation onsite include:
	Normal Pentane (CAS #109-66-0)
	Isopentane (CAS #78-78-4)
	Isopentane/n-Pentane Blends

Transloading Process
Our transloading process is designed to ensure the safe and complete transfer of chemicals from donating vessel to receiving vessel via a transloading skid that pumps the chemicals through the transfer line while also measuring quantity of chemica

l transferred. Because of the characteristics of Pentane and Isopentane, our employees observe certain safety precautions to prevent unnecessary human and environmental exposure, both within the terminal and in the surrounding community.

As required by the EPAs Risk Management regulation, we have identified scenarios that could result in the release of Pentane or Isopentane to the environment. Although possible, these scenarios are unlikely to occur at the Texas Deepwater Terminal for several reasons:
	We meet or exceed industry standards for the manufacture and quality control of hoses and vessels that contain Pentane and Isopentane used at our facility.
	Pentane and Isopentane is not corrosive in the form in which it is handled at the terminal.
	Process logic controllers limit operating flow, minimizing the chances of a large-scale release.
	Lower Explosive Limit (LEL) sensors warn of leaks.
	Safety valves allow the immediate shut-off of the transloading system and vessels donating or receiving chemicals.
	Equipment is inspected and kept in proper working order and replaced when necessary.
	The terminal has an emergency response plan and equipment in place.

Accidental Release Prevention Program
Texas Deepwater Partners has years of experience operating transloading processes at its terminals. This experience has informed designs and operating plans that ensure safe operation. The following elements have contributed to our safe operating record:
	Process hazard analysis and review, including corrective action follow-up.
	Standard operating procedures that all transloading process operators must follow.
	Formal operator training.
	Preventive maintenance to ensure the transloading system remains mechanically sound.
	Management of change procedures to maintain transloading flow safety.
	Safety reviews prior to startup of new or modified equipment.
	Audits of the PSM and RMP programs.
	Incident investigations to identify and apply lessons learned.
	E

mployee involvement in risk reduction efforts.
	Contractor safety procedures that meet terminal standards.
	A hot work permit system for safe welding practices.
	Thorough process safety information.
	Emergency planning and response measures.

The terminal complies with EPAs RMP rule (40 CFR 68), and OSHAs PSM standard (29 CFR 1910.119), including:

1.	Introduction to Process Safety Management
2.	Employee Involvement in Process Safety Management
3.	Process Safety Information
4.	Process Hazard Analysis
5.	Operating Procedures and Practices
6.	Employee Training
7.	Contractors
8.	Pre-Startup Safety
9.	Mechanical Integrity
10.	Nonroutine Work Authorizations
11.	Managing Change
12.	Investigation of Incidents
13.	Emergency Preparedness
14.	Compliance Audits

Five-Year Accident History
The terminal is a new operation and thus has had no incidents on-site.

Emergency Response Program
The facility maintains an onsite Emergency Action Plan (EAP) fully compliant with OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38 and EPA 40 CFR 68 requirements. The EAP outlines roles, responsibilities, evacuation procedures, communication protocols, emergency contacts, and external emergency coordination. For complete emergency response details, refer to the Texas Deepwater Terminal Emergency Response Plan dated May 21, 2025.

Key Emergency Contacts:
	Channelview Fire Department: 911 / Non-emergency main 281-452-5782
	CURA Environmental: 800-579-2872
	Jon Harris, Terminal SR Director: 713-249-5399
	Ron Percival, HSSE Sr. Director: 832-563-2937

Planned Changes to Improve Safety
The transloading process at the Texas Deepwater Terminal is periodically reviewed to enhance safety. All process components are maintained according to accepted practices and manufacturer instruction, including removal, testing, rebuilding (if needed), and reinstallation.

Conclusion
Texas Deepwater Partners is pleased to share information about its established systems for safe operations with the residents of Houston. We believe the Ris

k Management Plan is a valuable tool for fostering communication with our neighbors. Although we are confident that significant Pentane or Isopentane releases are highly unlikely, we want the community to know we are prepared to respond quickly and effectively if one were to occur. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of safety and environmental excellence and continuing our strong track record.
